name: nanomsg-85856cb7-blind28
instr:
# Diagnosing nanomsg messaging failures without a test suite

The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits.

A program built on this messaging library creates endpoints, points them at addresses, and moves messages between them, and it now gets a great many of those steps wrong. Nothing on the network changed and no caller changed. Work that used to go through is now mishandled, and in several places an operation that used to succeed fails outright, dies, or hangs.

Someone asking a receiving endpoint to take only messages that start with a chosen run of bytes finds that the call setting that option comes back as a failure, so the interest cannot be registered that way at all. Where one is already in place, a message whose leading bytes do match it is swallowed instead of being handed up: the receiving call behaves as if nothing had arrived and goes on waiting. Registering one whose bytes run out exactly where the stored set of them already branches files it in the wrong place, so later messages are matched against prefixes nobody asked for while the ones that were asked for are missed. Withdrawing one again reads from in front of the bytes it was given, and the stored set comes out mangled or the withdrawal reports that it was never there.

Setting the reply deadline on an endpoint that puts a single question to all of its peers and gathers their answers is refused with EINVAL when the value is handed over as a plain integer, and only a value of some other widt
